cycle_position.summary: Demand inflection: occupancy 89.9% in Q2 2026 (+0.4pp, record occupied units); NIC expects >90% in 2026 — a 20-year high — as the oldest boomers turn 80 this year and new supply stays scarce. Cap rates compressed to a 6.2% average through year-end 2025 (210 bps over the 10Y vs a 416 bps long-term average) and 85% of surveyed investors expect further compression.

supply_demand.value: Occupancy 89.9% and climbing; construction starts scarce; boomer-turning-80 demand wave begins 2026.

debt_terms.value: HUD 232 / agency seniors programs at institutional scale; small residential-assisted-living homes finance as residential + SBA.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: Direct = an operating healthcare business (staffing, licensure, liability) — not this buyer's game. The only $1-2M door: a residential assisted-living house (8-16 beds) WITH an experienced operator partner, or REIT/fund exposure to ride the demographic wave passively.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: The best demand story in real estate for the next decade, but the real product is care operations; real estate is the container. A hands-on value-add landlord skill set does not transfer to census management and state licensure.

gaps: DC/MD/VA residential assisted living licensure regimes (needed before any RAL-house consideration)
